exposure_report.A: the rule's four features are all richly present in train; holding out cells holds out COMBINATIONS, not rule components; R7 (a 4-feature lookup from train) reaches its registered score on unseen cells with no hand truth table. Refusal observations are asserted disjoint across splits, and eval refusal TYPE CLASSES (float-equal-to-int, string) are unseen in train -- disclosed.
exposure_report.C: measured: dev/eval strings verbatim in train = stats.C.verbatim_in_train (must be 0); dev/eval chains that contain a verbatim train chain as a sub-expression = stats.C.contain_a_verbatim_train_chain_as_subexpression -- disclosed, expected high, because every long chain extends a short one. The digit-multiset check used in v0.1 was vacuous and is gone.
exposure_report.G: strict topologies: none shared across splits by construction (asserted); all leaf literals recur -- disclosed; eval depths >= 4 are longer than anything in train.
exposure_report.R: strict shapes: none shared across splits by construction (asserted). Atomic literals, names and coefficients recur across splits -- disclosed. Eval and dev are small because the SDG pool has few strict shapes; see stats.R.

family_labels.A: CONFORMANCE AND TRANSFER, NOT DISCOVERY. The answer depends only on four field equalities (op==0, same_domain, target_noetic==op, source==target). A three-line hand rule (R3) and a 4-feature lookup filled from train (R7) are registered; a learned module is measured on fidelity to them and on transfer to unseen cells, and MUST report the order-flip and swapped-twin metrics and refusal accuracy on unseen refusal classes. Accuracy alone is not a claim.
family_labels.C: CONFORMANCE-ONLY. The modular-sum rule scores 1.0 by construction.
family_labels.G: STRUCTURAL GENERALISATION. Grammar-generated nested binary trees, compiled, held out by whole strict TOPOLOGY and by depth (eval prefers depth >= 4). This is the structural test R cannot be.
family_labels.R: FIDELITY. Expression -> canonical AST for SDG expressions. Ceiling = the compiler (measured). The SDG pool is structurally narrow; strict-shape holdout therefore yields a SMALL eval and dev, reported in stats. Reviewer measurement on v0.1: one regular expression reproduced 204/256 eval targets; 52/256 needed a grammar.

record_id_policy: sha256 of the raw UTF-8 string '<seed>:<family>:<split>:<index>', first 24 hex. Position only.
review_of_v0_1: three independent attackers, 2026-09-21: leak (refusals recycled), baseline (hand rule 1.0, lookup 1.0, order-flip rows 11.7%), split (R shape was a fingerprint; C dev not deduplicated). All three succeeded; v0.2 answers each by name in the module docstring.
sdg_usage: expression strings only; SDG prompt/response text is never read (the label sits inside it)
seal_policy: a file boundary against a LEARNER, not a secret: the sealed side regenerates from this public code and seed (shown by the v0.1 reviewers).

split_policy.A: whole (operator, source_domain, target_domain) cells: 24 eval, 16 dev, 120 train; eval/dev valid rows are >= 50% order-flip; refusals drawn from split-disjoint value pools and type classes
split_policy.C: one seen-set across all splits, train first; depths train 1-3, dev 2-3, eval 4-6
split_policy.G: whole strict topologies; eval takes depth>=4 topologies first, then rarest; dev the rarest of the rest
split_policy.R: whole STRICT shapes (every scalar leaf abstracted); eval then dev take the rarest first

supersedes: data/q3_v0_1 (kept on disk; reviewed and found leaking on 2026-09-21)

visibility.teacher_forcing_note: a target may be used to compute training LOSS; it is never a model INPUT at evaluated prediction; teacher-forced passes are not free-running reconstruction and are reported apart
